You are the architect for a feature on FirstRun's Doc-audit (repo: D:\Atharva\firstrun; Python 3.11 CLI plus a static site in docs/). Produce an implementation PLAN only (you cannot edit files). Another Opus agent will execute your plan, so be concrete: exact files, functions, data schemas, formulas, UI structure. Read the real code and data before planning: src/firstrun/audit.py (git history reading, read_history, find_features, momentum, build_cards, the `cards`/`features`/`pages`/`history` result fields, publish(), jev usage), src/firstrun/cli.py (audit commands), scripts/audit_intake.py and .github/workflows/audit-request.yml (the CI path that audits public repos on GitHub Actions), docs/doc-audit/index.html (the whole board UI: header, bar, the "What to Ship Next" four-column board with the drawer), docs/audits/*.json and docs/audits/index.json (7 real published audits: fastapi/typer, AltimateAI/altimate-code, entireio/cli, dbt-labs/dbt-core with docs repo dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com, OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator, neatlogs/neatlogs, AccuKnox/help), tests/test_audit.py and tests/test_intake.py, PRODUCT.md (design principles: calm, precise, Apple-like, light mode, one idea per section, H2s centered with NO subtitle, links underlined, never confusing) and docs/index.html for the visual language (three tinted bands, receipt bill, prism hero is being added elsewhere).

THE OWNER'S REQUEST (verbatim intent):
(1) In the Doc-audit "What to Ship Next" board the "Create Content" column "looks very silly, is not accurate and does not show real, valuable info" (it lists 'areas' like mkdocs, build, post, edit_template with '1 commit' each). Also "Document This" and "Create Content" "should be a single column ideally". Replace it with: "the TOP 10 PRIORITIZED issues to pick up next, with rationale".
(2) A team map: "show which user or contributor from GitHub has expertise in which part of the app so the relevant issues can be assigned to people who show proficiency in some part of the codebase: map the users to the task and show the distribution of that visually: team member X works most on Y, and suggest which issues to be picked by which team member. All this can be done via the GitHub contributor details." Place it "near the top of the audit page, before What to Ship Next, in a very amazing manner. This has to be visually amazing!"

WHAT YOUR PLAN MUST COVER
A. DATA MODEL (additive to audit.json schema v1; old boards must keep rendering): a `team` block and a `next` (top-10) block. Define exactly the fields. The audit already clones the repo (blobless, full history) and `read_history` yields per-commit author info and changed files: decide what author identity the history gives (name, email) and how to derive a GitHub login and avatar WITHOUT secrets: for example the `ID+login@users.noreply.github.com` noreply form, and optionally the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/contributors`, and commit author lookup) when a token exists (it does in GitHub Actions and on the owner's machine via `gh auth`), with a no-token fallback to initials and a deterministic color. Never publish email addresses on the public boards; hash or drop them. Exclude bots (dependabot, renovate, github-actions, copilot, *-bot, [bot]) and optionally merge commits. Merge identities that are clearly the same person (same login or same normalized name).
B. EXPERTISE ALGORITHM: define AREAS of the codebase (top-level directories or the existing `area` classification used by features and cards; for repos where docs live in a second repo such as dbt-core + docs.getdbt.com, say how areas map across both repos), and a recency-weighted expertise score per (person, area): for example exponential decay with a half-life of about 90 days on commits, weighted by lines or files changed with caps, normalized so one giant commit cannot dominate; derive `works most on`, `share of area`, `last active`, `bus factor` per area (how many people hold more than 20% of recent weight), and flag single-owner areas. Give the formulas and the thresholds, and justify them. Handle small repos (1 to 3 contributors), huge repos (hundreds of contributors: show top N plus an "everyone else" bucket), one-person repos (the map must still be meaningful and honest), and areas with no recent activity.
C. TOP 10 PRIORITIZED ISSUES with rationale: build them from the signals the audit already has (stale pages with commits since last edit, shipped user-facing features with no docs, momentum areas, release notes missing, quickstart check) and rank with an explicit scoring formula (impact for readers, urgency/staleness, effort, evidence strength, whether Jev judged it). Each item: a title in plain words, a one-sentence RATIONALE that cites its evidence (commit short SHAs, dates, counts), a priority score and a human-readable "why now", an effort estimate (S, M, L) with its rule, the suggested owner (person with the highest expertise in the touched area, tie-broken by recent activity and by balancing load so one person is not assigned everything), the runner-up, and a one-line reason ("Maya made 14 of the last 20 commits to docs/use-cases"). Only real data. If no one has expertise, say "no clear owner" and suggest the most recent toucher.
D. UI SPEC (this is the star: "visually amazing"): propose and justify the best visualization of "who works on what". Evaluate options such as a contributor by area heatmap matrix, a ribbon/chord or Sankey from people to areas, an arc or radial map, avatar-bubbles clustered by area, a stacked bar per area showing ownership share, a swimlane. Choose a primary view and a secondary view, specify the layout in detail (sizes, order, grouping, color system consistent with the site, labeling so a stranger understands it in 5 seconds without a legend lecture), hover and focus interactions (hover a person to highlight their areas and their suggested tasks; hover an area to see its owners), the connection to the Top 10 list (each item shows a small avatar of its suggested owner; clicking an owner filters the list to their picks), a bus-factor callout, empty and loading and error states, small-repo and huge-repo behavior, dark/light (site is light), responsive down to 375 px, keyboard and screen-reader support (tables or lists with the same information as text), reduced motion, performance (inline SVG or CSS grid, no libraries, board JSON size budget), and how the section is placed: after the board header and summary bar, BEFORE the ship-next list, with a centered H2 and no subtitle. The ship-next board becomes ONE column: the ranked top 10 as a clean list (rank number, title, rationale, evidence chips, effort, owner avatar), with the old kind filters kept only if they add value; say what happens to the other card kinds (refresh, feature, document, quickstart, automate) so nothing real is lost, and how the drawer that shows the commits behind a card is kept.
E. BACKFILL AND CI: how the 7 published boards get `team` and `next` WITHOUT re-running Jev or republishing changed counts (a script that re-clones, computes only the new blocks and writes them into docs/audits/<id>.json, in the style of scripts/audit_cost_estimates.py), how `firstrun audit` and the intake workflow produce them for new audits (GitHub token availability in Actions: GITHUB_TOKEN), rate-limit handling, caching, timeouts, and failure behavior (the audit must never fail because the contributor lookup failed).
F. PRIVACY AND ETHICS: this puts named people next to tasks on a public page. State what is shown (public commit authorship only, GitHub login and avatar, no emails), how a repo owner or a person can opt out (for example a `team: false` option, an env flag, a CLI flag `--no-team`), the wording that frames suggestions as suggestions, and that private-repo audits keep the board private as today.
G. TESTS: offline pytest plan with small synthetic git repos built in tmp_path (multiple authors, bots, noreply emails, renamed files, merge commits, a one-person repo, a repo with 300 authors), asserting the scores, the owner suggestion, load balancing, no emails in output, schema additivity (old board JSON still renders), and the front-end data contract.
H. WORK BREAKDOWN: an ordered list of steps with files touched, so one executing agent (or two in parallel: backend data, frontend UI) can implement and verify it. List risks, open questions that truly block, and a definition of done with how to verify in a browser (desktop 1280, tablet 768, phone 375) using the real published boards.

Be decisive: where there are options, pick one and say why. Keep the plan precise and compact enough to execute (aim for a document an engineer can follow without asking you anything). Do not write code files, but include short code or pseudo-code for the formulas and the JSON schema.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

schema.name: SearchPlugins
schema.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

keywords.description: Keyword phrases describing the user's intent.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

## cfoai
# cfo.ai MCP

You are connected to **cfo.ai** — an AI-native financial planning workspace. This MCP exposes Ari's public product tools for you to call directly. You can both **read** a company's financial model and **change** it: create and edit scenarios, pages, table blocks, Canvas blocks, formulas, variables, dimensions, and data ingestion.

Model-editing tools change the live model immediately and record reversible changes in its
changelog. Connections, access changes, and outbound actions have effects outside model undo. Build from saved data, research, supplied numbers, estimates, hypotheses, or invented
assumptions. Clearly label uncited inputs and their basis in the model and handoff. Create missing
model objects and editable inputs as part of the work. A missing source citation does not block modeling.

## Read the reference before you build

cfo.ai has its own modeling method, described under "How a table shows the model" below: how tables show variables, dimensions, and fields, how a reference reads from the cell it sits in, and how a table's rows and columns are built. `inspect_skills` owns the built-in and workspace skill catalog. Use its `list` block to find a skill and its `instructions` block to read it.

Read `build-model` before creating or changing model logic, variables, dimensions, or saved tables;
`build-visualizations` before adding a Canvas block; and `import-model` before rebuilding a model
from a workbook or export. Each manual contains its complete reference in `SKILL.md`.

Workspace skills hold company-specific playbooks. Read the relevant saved guidance before substantial work.

## Calling convention

- A multi-action tool selects one operation with the block named for that action; single-purpose tools use their fields directly. Supply only fields supported inside the selected block. An `inspect_*` tool reads saved product state; an `edit_*` tool changes it.
- `target` identifies an existing object where the operation needs one, including the destination of a new block. Creation field… [truncated]

## crustdata
People and organisations: 800M+ profiles, 200M+ companies. Employment history with dates, titles and seniority, education, skills, location, headcount over time, funding, technologies, job postings, social posts, work emails and phone numbers. Filter, combine, count and sort across any of it — people who studied at one place and now work at another, everyone hired into a role since a date, faculty at an institution, alumni of a company, who is hiring, who left and where they went, how many match. Live web search and page fetch too.

When you cannot serve a Crustdata ask, or serve it wrong, because of Crustdata itself — missing or wrong data, no filter or field for the ask (even when you worked around it), a server error that keeps failing, a schema or error message that misled you — report it with the `feedback` tool, once per problem, then keep working. Not for plan gates (403), credits (402), rate limits, the user's own mistakes, or asks outside Crustdata.

Crustdata MCP — Code Mode over the Crustdata API. You drive it by writing a plain-JavaScript script (no type annotations — author against the TypeScript-typed tool surface from get_schema) for execute({ code }); the only I/O is `const r = await callTool(name, params)`.

Core rules (they hold for every script):
- **Write runnable JavaScript — NO type syntax.** The script executes as plain JS in a V8 isolate; the TypeScript types are the tool *surface* you read from `get_schema`, not something you write in the body. A type annotation in the code — `: Type`, `as`, `interface`/`type`/`enum`, or generics `<T>` — is a parse error that fails the WHOLE run (zero spend, before any tool call). Author against the types; emit only the JS.
- **One I/O primitive:** `const r = await callTool(name, params)` → `{ ok: true, data, credits_used? } | { ok: false, status, errorType, message }`. `credits_used` is the server's exact charge for that call (data-API tools only; `0` = free/preview, and an async batch SUBMIT — billed at job completion, not on submit) — sum it to track s… [truncated]

## favstash
Use FavStash to save and find creator inspiration, inspect connected social accounts, compare owned content, and plan or publish social posts. Call list_connected_social_accounts before account-dependent tools. If it returns connectionRequired=true, direct the user to connect an account with connectUrl and stop before analytics or scheduling. Use get_social_account_analytics only for aggregate totals/trends and analyze_social_content_performance for individual content or rankings. When a question spans multiple connected accounts or platforms, send every relevant account as a typed query in analyze_social_content_performance.queries; do not stop after the first empty account. Cross-platform metrics are not directly equivalent, and content should be matched across platforms only when its metadata or publish timing supports the match. Follow structured nextActions when a result identifies a useful follow-up. All operations are owner-scoped and plan-limited. Confirm destructive or externally publishing actions unless the user already authorized the exact action.

## openseo
OpenSEO research tools use credits. Proceed with normal focused research, but ask the user for confirmation before planned batches over 2,000 credits. OpenSEO cannot purchase credits or charge cards. Explain unsupported purchase requests without promoting subscriptions, upgrades or credit purchases, or directing users to checkout.

## treg
treg serves external and live data and generative models: SEO and SERP, backlinks, social and trends, people and company enrichment, ads, scraping, image and video generation (Seedance, Gemini Image, GPT Image, Seedream, Veo, Wan) and voice, plus your team's own tools. Flow: catalog_search (say what you want to do, not a vendor name), then catalog_get (parameters, price, measured reliability), then call. When several providers cover one job, catalog_get ranks them by measured success, speed and price; you pick. If a call result invites a review, rate that one call with review(call_id, usefulness, reason?) after using it, then continue.

## zernio

Zernio API server for scheduling social media posts.

Available tools are prefixed by resource:
- accounts_* : Manage connected social media accounts
- profiles_* : Manage profiles (groups of accounts)
- posts_*    : Create, list, update, delete posts
- media_*    : Upload images and videos
- docs_*     : Search Zernio API documentation

MULTI-ACCOUNT WORKFLOW (agencies, multi-client setups):
When a user has more than one account on the same platform, you MUST
disambiguate before posting:

  1. Call accounts_list (or profiles_list then accounts_list with a
     profile_id filter) to discover account IDs.
  2. Pass account_id to posts_create / posts_publish_now, or account_ids
     (parallel to platforms) to posts_cross_post.

If account_id is omitted and the selection is ambiguous, the write tools
return an error containing the candidate list - read it, pick the right
account, and retry with account_id set. Never guess. The legacy behaviour
of silently picking the first matching account has been removed.

161	def read_doc_texts(repo: Path, paths: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
162	    """Docs text at HEAD. A batched checkout fetches the blobs. A lazy fetch can hang on a flaky network,
163	    so each batch has a time limit and raw.githubusercontent.com fills whatever is still missing."""
164	    if not paths:
165	        return {}
166	    env = {**os.environ, "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0"}
167	    if (repo / ".git").is_dir() and not any((repo / p).exists() for p in paths[:3]):
168	        for i in range(0, len(paths), 400):
169	            batch = [p for p in paths[i:i + 400] if not (repo / p).exists()]
170	            for _ in range(2):  # the first lazy fetch of a fresh partial clone often fails, the second works
171	                if not batch:
172	                    break
173	                try:
174	                    # No `-c` here: a config override on the command line breaks the lazy blob fetch.
175	                    r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "checkout", "HEAD", "--", *batch], capture_output=True,
176	                                       text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=90, env=env)
177	                    if r.returncode == 0:
178	                        break
179	                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
180	                    pass
181	                batch = [p for p in batch if not (repo / p).exists()]
182	    out = {}
183	    for p in paths:
184	        try:
185	            out[p] = (repo / p).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
186	        except OSError:
187	            out[p] = None
188	    missing = [p for p, t in out.items() if t is None]
189	    base = _raw_base(repo) if missing else ""
190	    if missing and base:
191	        from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
192	
193	        def get(path: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
194	            try:
195	                r = httpx.get(base + quote(path), timeout=20)
196	                return path, r.text if r.status_code == 200 else ""
197	            except httpx.HTTPError:
198	                return path, ""
199	
200	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as pool:
201	            for path, text in pool.map(get, missing):
202	                out[path] = text
203	    return {p: (t or "") for p, t in out.items()}

208	def _title(text: str, path: str) -> str:
209	    for pat in (r"^title:\s*[\"']?(.+?)[\"']?\s*$", r"^#\s+(.+)$"):
210	        m = re.search(pat, text[:4000], re.M)
211	        t = re.sub(r"[`*_\[\]]|<[^>]*>|\{[^}]*\}", "", m.group(1)).strip() if m else ""
212	        if t and not t.startswith(("<", "{", "!")):
213	            return t[:100]

217	def _keywords(path: str, title: str) -> set[str]:
218	    """The page's topic words: its file name, or its folder when the file is an index page."""
219	    parts = Path(path.lower()).with_suffix("").parts
220	    name = parts[-1] if parts else ""
221	    if name in GENERIC and len(parts) > 1:
222	        name = parts[-2]
223	    words = re.findall(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]{2,}", name)
224	    keep = {w for w in words if w not in GENERIC and w not in STOP and w not in {"md", "mdx", "rst", "adoc", "and", "with", "for"}}
225	    return {w[:-1] if len(w) > 4 and w.endswith("s") and not w.endswith("ss") else w for w in keep}

228	def analyze_pages(commits: list[dict], docs: list[str], texts: dict[str, str], now: datetime,
229	                  stale_days: int, product_commits: list[dict] | None = None, repo_name: str = "") -> list[dict]:
230	    """commits holds the docs history. product_commits holds the code history when docs live in another repo."""
231	    docset = set(docs)
232	    last: dict[str, dict] = {}
233	    for c in commits:  # newest first, so the first sight of a file is its last touch
234	        for f in c["files"]:
235	            if f in docset and f not in last:
236	                last[f] = c
237	    # Only user-facing change counts as the product moving: bumps, CI and refactors do not.
238	    product = [c for c in (commits if product_commits is None else product_commits) if any(_is_product(f) for f in c["files"])
239	               and classify_subject(c["subject"]) not in ("internal", "docs")]
240	    # Precompute once: each product commit's topic tokens, and its date for a bisect.
241	    toks = []
242	    for p in product:
243	        hay = " ".join(f.lower() for f in p["files"] if _is_product(f)) + " " + " ".join(
244	            re.findall(r"`([^`]+)`", p["subject"].lower())) + " " + (p.get("scope") or "")
245	        words = set(re.findall(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*", hay))
246	        toks.append(words | {w[:-1] for w in words if len(w) > 4 and w.endswith("s")})
247	    neg_dates = [-p["date"].timestamp() for p in product]  # product is newest first, so this ascends
248	    # A topic word that shows up in more than 2% of product commits ("column", "src") names no topic.
249	    df = Counter(w for t in toks for w in t)
250	    # Small projects keep every word: with under 200 commits, one area can fairly own most of them.
251	    rare = int(0.02 * len(product)) if len(product) >= 200 else len(product)
252	    pages = []
253	    for path in docs:
254	        c = last.get(path)
255	        title = _title(texts.get(path, ""), path)
256	        # The project's own name matches every commit, so it never marks a topic.
257	        kw = _keywords(path, title) - set(re.findall(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]{2,}", repo_name.lower()))
258	        kw = {k for k in kw if 0 < df[k] <= rare}
259	        if c is None:  # touched before the history window
260	            touched = None
261	            age = (now - commits[-1]["date"]).days if commits else 0
262	        else:
263	            touched = c["date"]
264	            age = max(0, (now - touched).days)
265	        n_since = len(product) if touched is None else bisect.bisect_left(neg_dates, -touched.timestamp())
266	        since = product[:n_since]
267	        relevant = [p for p, t in zip(since, toks) if kw and not kw.isdisjoint(t)]
268	        if age < 90:
269	            status = "fresh"
270	        elif age < stale_days:
271	            status = "aging"
272	        elif relevant:
273	            status = "stale"
274	        else:
275	            status = "quiet"
276	        pages.append({
277	            "path": path, "title": title,
278	            "last_touched": touched.date().isoformat() if touched else None,
279	            "age_days": age, "older_than_history": touched is None,
280	            "status": status, "ancient": age >= 730,
281	            "relevant_since": len(relevant), "product_since": len(since),
282	            "last_commit": (c["subject"][:100] if c else ""),
283	            "evidence": [{"sha": p["sha"][:9], "date": p["date"].date().isoformat(), "subject": p["subject"][:100]}
284	                         for p in relevant[:3]],
285	        })
286	    pages.sort(key=lambda p: (-p["age_days"], p["path"]))
287	    return pages

321	def jev_stale(pages: list[dict], texts: dict[str, str]) -> int:
322	    """Jev reads each stale candidate and the commits behind it. Only a page Jev expects a commit to break stays
323	    stale. When Jev ran, candidates it never read become "unchecked", because text matching alone over-claims.
324	    Returns how many pages Jev cleared. Changes nothing when Jev is unavailable."""
325	    config.load_env()
326	    key = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_API_KEY")
327	    cand = sorted([p for p in pages if p["status"] == "stale"], key=lambda p: -p.get("relevant_since", 0))
328	    if not key or not cand:
329	        return 0
330	    checked, cleared, ran = set(), 0, False
331	    todo = cand[:JEV_STALE_MAX]
332	    for i in range(0, len(todo), JEV_BATCH):
333	        batch = todo[i:i + JEV_BATCH]
334	        got = _jev_stale_batch(key, batch, texts)
335	        if got is None:
336	            continue
337	        ran = True
338	        for j, prob in got.items():
339	            p = batch[j]
340	            p["stale_p"] = round(prob, 2)
341	            p["judge"] = "jev"
342	            checked.add(p["path"])
343	            if prob < STALE_P:
344	                p["status"] = "quiet"
345	                cleared += 1
346	    if ran:
347	        for p in cand:
348	            if p["path"] not in checked:
349	                p["status"] = "unchecked"
350	    return cleared

364	def classify_subject(subject: str) -> str:
365	    """feature, fix, docs, internal or unknown, from the subject line alone. Reads gitmoji too."""
366	    s = re.sub(r"\s*\(#\d+\)\s*$", "", subject.strip())
367	    for emoji, kind in _GITMOJI.items():
368	        if s.startswith(emoji):
369	            return kind
370	    s = re.sub(r"^:[a-z_]+:\s*", "", s)
371	    m = _CONV.match(s)
372	    if m:
373	        t = m.group("t").lower()
374	        if t in _FEATURE_T:
375	            return "feature"
376	        if t in _FIX_T:
377	            return "fix"
378	        if t in _DOCS_T:
379	            return "docs"
380	        if t in _INTERNAL_T:
381	            return "internal"
382	    if _INTERNAL_WORDS.match(s) or s.lower().startswith(("merge ", "revert ")):
383	        return "internal"
384	    if _FEATURE_WORDS.match(s):
385	        return "feature"
386	    if _FIX_WORDS.match(s):
387	        return "fix"
388	    return "unknown"

391	_CRITERIA = {
392	    "feature": "A user can now do something new, or a new option, command, integration or capability shipped.",
393	    "fix": "A bug, crash or wrong behavior was corrected.",
394	    "docs": "Only documentation changed.",
395	    "internal": "Refactor, tests, CI, dependency bump or tooling that users never see.",

399	def jev_sort(subjects: list[str]) -> dict[int, str]:
400	    """One Jev call, one Choice question per commit subject. Returns {index: class}. Empty on any failure."""
401	    config.load_env()
402	    key = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_API_KEY")
403	    if not key or not subjects:
404	        return {}
405	    body = {
406	        "model": JEV_MODEL,
407	        "state": {"commit_subjects": {str(i): s for i, s in enumerate(subjects)}},
408	        "questions": {f"c{i}": {"type": "choice",
409	                                "instructions": f"What kind of change is commit subject number {i} in this open-source project?",
410	                                "criteria": _CRITERIA} for i in range(len(subjects))},
411	    }
412	    try:
413	        r = httpx.post(JEV_URL, json=body, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, timeout=60)
414	        r.raise_for_status()
415	        answers = _note_jev(r.json())["answers"]
416	        out = {}
417	        for i in range(len(subjects)):
418	            probs = answers[f"c{i}"]["probabilities"]
419	            best = max(probs, key=probs.get)
420	            if best in _CRITERIA and probs[best] >= 0.5:
421	                out[i] = best
422	        return out
423	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - Jev is optional
424	        return {}

427	def _terms(subject: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
428	    """(strong terms, weak words). Strong terms are flags, backticked names and identifiers."""
429	    s = re.sub(r"\s*\(#\d+\)\s*$", "", subject)
430	    s = _CONV.sub(lambda m: m.group("m"), s.strip(), count=1)
431	    strong = re.findall(r"`([^`]{2,40})`", s) + re.findall(r"(?<![\w-])(--[a-z][\w-]{2,})", s)
432	    # Identifiers only. A hyphenated word in prose ("locally-authored") is English, not a name a page would carry.
433	    strong += [w for w in re.findall(r"\b[a-z]+[A-Z][A-Za-z]+\b|\b[a-z]+_[a-z_]+\b|\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+_[A-Z0-9_]+\b", s)]
434	    weak = [w for w in re.findall(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]{3,}", s.lower()) if w not in STOP]
435	    return list(dict.fromkeys(x.lower() for x in strong)), list(dict.fromkeys(weak))

443	def _excerpt(texts: dict[str, str], words: list[str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
444	    """(path, about 1,200 characters) of the docs page that shares the most words with a feature."""
445	    best, score = "", 0
446	    for path, t in texts.items():
447	        low = t.lower()
448	        k = sum(1 for w in words if w in low)
449	        if k > score:
450	            best, score = path, k
451	    if not best:
452	        return "", ""
453	    low = texts[best].lower()
454	    hits = [low.find(w) for w in words if w in low]
455	    at = max(0, min(hits) - 300) if hits else 0
456	    return best, texts[best][at:at + 1200]

488	def find_features(commits: list[dict], now: datetime, corpus: str, use_jev: bool,
489	                  texts: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
490	    window = now - timedelta(days=FEATURE_WINDOW_DAYS)
491	    recent = [c for c in commits if c["date"] >= window and any(_is_product(f) for f in c["files"])]
492	    kinds = [classify_subject(c["subject"]) for c in recent]
493	    if use_jev:
494	        idx = [i for i, k in enumerate(kinds) if k == "unknown"][:JEV_MAX]
495	        for i, k in jev_sort([recent[i]["subject"] for i in idx]).items():
496	            kinds[idx[i]] = k
497	    feats = []
498	    for c, k in zip(recent, kinds):
499	        if k != "feature":
500	            continue
501	        strong, weak = _terms(c["subject"])
502	        hits = [t for t in strong if t in corpus]
503	        if strong:
504	            covered = bool(hits)
505	        else:
506	            covered = bool(weak) and sum(1 for w in weak if w in corpus) >= max(2, len(weak) // 2 + 1)
507	        top = (strong or weak or [""])[0]
508	        m = _CONV.match(re.sub(r"^\W+", "", c["subject"]))
509	        pfiles = [f for f in c["files"] if _is_product(f)]
510	        stem = Path(pfiles[0]).stem.lower() if pfiles else ""
511	        area = (m.group("s") or "").lower() if m and m.group("s") else ""
512	        area_src = "scope" if area else ""
513	        if not area:
514	            area = stem if stem and stem not in GENERIC | {"__init__", "core", "main", "utils", "util", "lib"} else top
515	            area_src = "file" if area == stem else "term"
516	        feats.append({"sha": c["sha"][:9], "date": c["date"].date().isoformat(), "subject": c["subject"][:140],
517	                      "author": c["author"], "pr": _pr(c["subject"]), "term": top, "area": area, "area_src": area_src,
518	                      "strong": strong[:4], "covered": covered, "judge": "text",
519	                      "files": [f for f in c["files"] if _is_product(f)][:4], "_words": strong + weak})
520	    texts = texts or {}
521	    hint = [_excerpt(texts, f["_words"]) for f in feats]
522	    for f, (path, _) in zip(feats, hint):
523	        f["closest_page"] = path
524	    if use_jev and feats:
525	        top = feats[:JEV_MAX]
526	        verdict = jev_features(top, [h[1] for h in hint[:JEV_MAX]])
527	        for i, (kind, p_cov) in verdict.items():
528	            top[i]["jev_kind"] = kind
529	            top[i]["covered"] = p_cov >= 0.5
530	            top[i]["judge"] = "jev"
531	        feats = [f for f in feats if f.get("jev_kind", "feature") == "feature"]
532	    for f in feats:
533	        f.pop("_words", None)
534	    return feats

537	def momentum(commits: list[dict], now: datetime, feats: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:
538	    """Commits and authors that touch the same term in the window. Three or more commits is momentum."""
539	    window = now - timedelta(days=FEATURE_WINDOW_DAYS)
540	    out = {}
541	    for f in feats:
542	        t = f["area"]
543	        if not t or t in out:
544	            continue
545	        rel = [c for c in commits if c["date"] >= window and classify_subject(c["subject"]) not in ("internal", "docs")
546	               and t in (c["subject"].lower() + " " + " ".join(x for x in c["files"] if _is_product(x)).lower())]
547	        out[t] = {"commits": len(rel), "authors": len({c["author"] for c in rel})}
548	    return out

556	def release_range(commits: list[dict], tags: list[dict], now: datetime) -> dict:
557	    """The newest stable release and the commits in it. Falls back to the last 30 days when there are no tags."""
558	    stable = [t for t in tags if not _PRE.search(t["name"])]
559	    tags = stable or tags
560	    if len(tags) >= 2:
561	        newest, prev = tags[0], tags[1]
562	        sel = [c for c in commits if prev["date"] < c["date"] <= newest["date"] + timedelta(hours=1)]
563	        return {"name": newest["name"], "previous": prev["name"], "date": newest["date"].date().isoformat(), "commits": sel}
564	    if len(tags) == 1:
565	        sel = [c for c in commits if c["date"] <= tags[0]["date"] + timedelta(hours=1)][:60]
566	        return {"name": tags[0]["name"], "previous": "", "date": tags[0]["date"].date().isoformat(), "commits": sel}
567	    sel = [c for c in commits if c["date"] >= now - timedelta(days=30)]
568	    return {"name": "Unreleased", "previous": "", "date": now.date().isoformat(), "commits": sel}

571	def _clean(subject: str) -> str:
572	    s = re.sub(r"\s*\(#\d+\)\s*$", "", subject.strip())
573	    s = re.sub(r"^(?::[a-z_]+:|[^\w`(\[]+)\s*", "", s)
574	    s = _CONV.sub(lambda m: m.group("m"), s, count=1)
575	    return s[:1].upper() + s[1:]

578	def draft_release_notes(repo_name: str, rel: dict, kinds: dict[str, str]) -> str:
579	    groups = defaultdict(list)
580	    for c in rel["commits"]:
581	        k = kinds.get(c["sha"]) or classify_subject(c["subject"])
582	        low = c["subject"].lower()
583	        if k == "internal" or low.startswith("merge ") or re.search(r"release notes|changelog|bump version|release version", low):
584	            continue
585	        pr = _pr(c["subject"])
586	        groups[k if k in ("feature", "fix", "docs") else "other"].append(
587	            f"- {_clean(c['subject'])}" + (f" (#{pr})" if pr else ""))
588	    names = [("feature", "New"), ("fix", "Fixed"), ("docs", "Docs"), ("other", "Also in this release")]
589	    lines = [f"# {repo_name} {rel['name']}", ""]
590	    if rel["previous"]:
591	        lines += [f"Changes since {rel['previous']}, released {rel['date']}.", ""]
592	    for key, title in names:
593	        if groups[key]:
594	            lines += [f"## {title}", "", *list(dict.fromkeys(groups[key]))[:25], ""]
595	    if len(lines) <= 3:
596	        lines.append("No user-facing changes found in this range.")
597	    lines.append("_Draft from the git history. Edit before you publish._")
598	    return "\n".join(lines).strip() + "\n"

624	def build_cards(repo: str, pages: list[dict], feats: list[dict], mom: dict[str, dict], rel: dict,
625	                notes: str, has_changelog_recent: bool, stale_days: int) -> list[dict]:
626	    cards: list[dict] = []
627	
628	    def ev(f):
629	        return {"sha": f["sha"], "date": f["date"], "subject": f["subject"], "pr": f["pr"]}
630	
631	    repo_words = set(re.findall(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]{2,}", repo.lower()))
632	    ordered = sorted(feats, key=lambda f: f["date"], reverse=True)
633	    ordered = sorted(ordered, key=lambda f: mom.get(f["area"], {}).get("commits", 0), reverse=True)
634	
635	    # Undocumented features that share an area become one card: a missing page, not 20 missing lines.
636	    unc = [f for f in ordered if not f["covered"]]
637	    by_area: dict[str, list[dict]] = defaultdict(list)
638	    for f in unc:
639	        by_area[f["area"]].append(f)
640	    clustered = set()
641	    for area, fs in sorted(by_area.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):
642	        if len(fs) < 3 or not area or len(area) < 3 or area in repo_words:
643	            continue
644	        clustered.add(area)
645	        near = Counter(f.get("closest_page") for f in fs if f.get("closest_page")).most_common(1)
646	        first = min(f["date"] for f in fs)
647	        judged = any(f.get("judge") == "jev" for f in fs)
648	        own = sorted((p["path"] for p in pages if area.lower() in p["path"].lower()), key=len)
649	        if own:
650	            title = f"Document the new `{area}` changes"
651	            why = (f"{len(fs)} user-facing changes to `{area}` shipped since {first}. "
652	                   + ("Jev read the closest docs page for each one and found none of them explained." if judged
653	                      else "No docs page names them."))
654	            action = f"Add them to {own[0]}, the `{area}` page, with one example each."
655	        else:
656	            title = f"Document the `{area}` feature"
657	            why = (f"{len(fs)} user-facing changes to `{area}` shipped since {first}, and no docs page is about `{area}`."
658	                   + (" Jev read the closest page for each change." if judged else ""))
659	            action = (f"Write one `{area}` page: what it does, how to turn it on, and its commands."
660	                      + (f" Link it from {near[0][0]}." if near else ""))
661	        cards.append({"kind": "document", "priority": 0, "title": title, "why": why, "action": action,
662	                      "evidence": [ev(f) for f in fs[:3]], "count": len(fs)})
663	    seen = set()
664	    for f in unc:
665	        if f["area"] in clustered or f["subject"] in seen:
666	            continue
667	        seen.add(f["subject"])
668	        cards.append({"kind": "document", "priority": 1, "title": f"Document: {_clean(f['subject'])}",
669	                      "why": (f"Shipped {f['date']}. Jev read the closest docs page and found it does not explain this."
670	                              if f.get("judge") == "jev" else f"Shipped {f['date']} and no docs page names `{f['term'] or 'it'}`. A user cannot find it."),
671	                      "action": (f"Add a section to {f['closest_page']}, the closest page, or write a short how-to and link it from the feature list."
672	                                 if f.get("closest_page") else "Write a short how-to page and link it from the feature list."),
673	                      "evidence": [ev(f)]})
674	
675	    # Content: areas the team keeps shipping. Projects that scope their commits get scopes only.
676	    use_scopes = sum(1 for f in feats if f.get("area_src") == "scope") >= max(3, len(feats) // 3)
677	    picks: dict[str, tuple[dict, dict]] = {}
678	    for f in ordered:
679	        a = f["area"]
680	        if not a or len(a) < 3 or a in repo_words or a in picks or (use_scopes and f.get("area_src") != "scope"):
681	            continue
682	        m = mom.get(a, {"commits": 1, "authors": 1})
683	        if m["commits"] >= 4 or (m["commits"] >= 3 and m["authors"] >= 2):
684	            picks[a] = (m, f)
685	    for a, (m, f) in sorted(picks.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1][0]["commits"]):
686	        cards.append({"kind": "content", "priority": 2, "title": f"Create content around `{a}`",
687	                      "why": f"{m['commits']} user-facing commits by {m['authors']} "
688	                             f"{'person' if m['authors'] == 1 else 'people'} touched it in {FEATURE_WINDOW_DAYS} days. "
689	                             "The team keeps investing here, so it is worth a story."
690	                             + (" It has no docs page yet, so write that first." if a in clustered else ""),
691	                      "action": "Publish a tutorial, a 60-second demo and a changelog post. Reuse the highlight draft below.",
692	                      "evidence": [ev(f)]})
693	    judged = [f for f in feats if f.get("judge") == "jev"]
694	    for f in (judged or feats)[:5]:
695	        if f["date"] >= (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=45)).date().isoformat():
696	            cards.append({"kind": "feature", "priority": 2, "title": f"Feature this: {_clean(f['subject'])}",
697	                          "why": f"Shipped {f['date']}. Recent and user-visible, so it belongs on the homepage and in the release post.",
698	                          "action": "Add it to the release post, the homepage feature list and the next newsletter.",
699	                          "evidence": [ev(f)]})
700	    for p in [x for x in pages if x["status"] == "stale"][:8]:
701	        cards.append({"kind": "refresh", "priority": 1 if p["ancient"] or p["relevant_since"] >= 5 else 3,
702	                      "title": f"Refresh {p['path']}",
703	                      "why": f"Last touched {p['last_touched'] or 'before the history window'} ({p['age_days']} days ago). "
704	                             f"Since then, {_n(p['relevant_since'], 'commit')} changed code on its topic, "
705	                             f"out of {_n(p['product_since'], 'user-facing commit')}.",
706	                      "action": ("Jev read the page and the commits and expects at least one to make it wrong or incomplete. "
707	                                 if p.get("judge") == "jev" else "") + "Re-read the page against the current code and update or delete what changed.",
708	                      "evidence": p["evidence"]})
709	    if rel["commits"]:
710	        cards.append({"kind": "automate", "priority": 2, "title": f"Release notes for {rel['name']} are ready to edit",
711	                      "why": f"{_n(len(rel['commits']), 'commit')} since {rel['previous'] or 'the last 30 days'}. "
712	                             + ("A changelog file changed recently." if has_changelog_recent else "No changelog file changed in this window."),
713	                      "action": "Open the draft, trim it, and publish it as the GitHub release body.", "evidence": []})
714	    cards.append({"kind": "quickstart", "priority": 3, "title": "Run the quickstart as a new developer",
715	                  "why": "An audit reads text. A run proves the steps still work in a clean container.",
716	                  "action": f"firstrun https://github.com/{repo}#readme", "evidence": []})
717	    caps = {"document": 8, "refresh": 6, "feature": 4, "content": 4}
718	    kept, used = [], Counter()
719	    for c in sorted(cards, key=lambda c: c["priority"]):
720	        if used[c["kind"]] < caps.get(c["kind"], 3):
721	            used[c["kind"]] += 1
722	            kept.append(c)
723	    return kept

762	def _audit(target: str, stale_days: int = 180, use_jev: bool = True, keep: Path | None = None,
763	           docs_repo: str | None = None) -> dict:
764	    """docs_repo: a second repo that holds the docs site, when the docs do not live next to the code."""
765	    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
766	    url, name = resolve_target(target)
767	    _JEV_USE.update(calls=0, input_tokens=0)
768	    tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="firstrun-audit-"))
769	    try:
770	        with neatlogs.trace("audit.clone", kind="TOOL") as span:
771	            repo = clone(url, keep or tmp / "repo")
772	            set_io(span, input={"repo": name})
773	        with neatlogs.trace("audit.history", kind="TOOL") as span:
774	            commits = read_history(repo)
775	            tags = read_tags(repo)
776	            set_io(span, output={"commits": len(commits), "tags": len(tags)})
777	        if not commits:
778	            raise RuntimeError("the repository has no commits")
779	        docs_url = f"https://github.com/{name}" if "/" in name and not Path(name).exists() else ""
780	        with neatlogs.trace("audit.pages", kind="TOOL") as span:
781	            if docs_repo:
782	                durl, dname = resolve_target(docs_repo)
783	                drepo = clone(durl, tmp / "docs")
784	                dcommits = read_history(drepo)
785	                docs = [f for f in _git(drepo, "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", "HEAD").splitlines()
786	                        if Path(f).suffix.lower() in DOC_EXT and not DOC_SKIP.search(f)]
787	                texts = read_doc_texts(drepo, docs)
788	                pages = analyze_pages(dcommits, docs, texts, now, stale_days, product_commits=commits, repo_name=name)
789	                docs_url = f"https://github.com/{dname}" if "/" in dname and not Path(dname).exists() else ""
790	            else:
791	                docs = head_docs(repo)
792	                texts = read_doc_texts(repo, docs)
793	                pages = analyze_pages(commits, docs, texts, now, stale_days, repo_name=name)
794	            cleared = jev_stale(pages, texts) if use_jev else 0
795	            set_io(span, input={"docs_repo": docs_repo or name}, output={**_summary(pages), "jev_cleared": cleared})
796	        corpus = " ".join(texts.values()).lower()
797	        with neatlogs.trace("audit.features", kind="TOOL") as span:
798	            feats = find_features(commits, now, corpus, use_jev, texts)
799	            mom = momentum(commits, now, feats)
800	            set_io(span, output={"features": len(feats), "uncovered": sum(1 for f in feats if not f["covered"])})
801	        rel = release_range(commits, tags, now)
802	        kinds = {c["sha"]: classify_subject(c["subject"]) for c in rel["commits"]}
803	        notes = draft_release_notes(name, rel, kinds)
804	        highlights = draft_highlights(name, feats, mom)
805	        cl = [c for c in commits if c["date"] >= now - timedelta(days=60)
806	              and any(re.search(r"(^|/)(changelog|history|changes|release[-_ ]?notes?)", f, re.I) for f in c["files"])]
807	        cards = build_cards(name, pages, feats, mom, rel, notes, bool(cl), stale_days)
808	        stamp = now.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
809	        result = {
810	            "v": 1, "id": f"audit-{stamp}-{re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', name.lower()).strip('-')}",
811	            "repo": name, "url": f"https://github.com/{name}" if "/" in name and not Path(name).exists() else "",
812	            "docs_repo": docs_repo or "", "docs_url": docs_url,
813	            "generated_at": now.isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "stale_days": stale_days,
814	            "history": {"commits": len(commits), "since": commits[-1]["date"].date().isoformat(),
815	                        "capped": len(commits) >= HISTORY_MAX, "head": commits[0]["sha"]},
816	            "summary": {**_summary(pages), "features": len(feats), "uncovered": sum(1 for f in feats if not f["covered"]),
817	                        "cards": len(cards)},
818	            "pages": pages[:PAGES_MAX],
819	            "release": {"name": rel["name"], "previous": rel["previous"], "date": rel["date"], "commits": len(rel["commits"])},
820	            "features": feats[:40], "cards": cards[:30],
821	            "drafts": {"release_notes": notes, "highlights": highlights},
822	            "jev": bool(use_jev and os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_API_KEY")),
823	            "cost": jev_cost(),
824	        }
825	        return result
826	    finally:
827	        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)

832	def audit_sitemap(site: str, stale_days: int = 180) -> dict:
833	    """A docs site with no repo: read the sitemap and rank pages by lastmod."""
834	    base = site.rstrip("/")
835	    if not base.startswith("http"):
836	        base = "https://" + base
837	    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
838	    xml = ""
839	    for path in ("/sitemap.xml", "/sitemap_index.xml"):
840	        try:
841	            r = httpx.get(base + path, timeout=20, follow_redirects=True)
842	            if r.status_code == 200 and "<url" in r.text:
843	                xml = r.text
844	                break
845	        except httpx.HTTPError:
846	            continue
847	    if not xml:
848	        raise RuntimeError("no sitemap.xml with <lastmod> dates found")
849	    pages = []
850	    for loc, mod in re.findall(r"<url>\s*<loc>([^<]+)</loc>(?:.*?<lastmod>([^<]+)</lastmod>)?", xml, re.S):
851	        if not mod:
852	            continue
853	        try:
854	            d = datetime.fromisoformat(mod.strip().replace("Z", "+00:00"))
855	        except ValueError:
856	            continue
857	        d = d if d.tzinfo else d.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
858	        age = max(0, (now - d).days)
859	        pages.append({"path": loc.strip(), "title": loc.strip().rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1] or loc,
860	                      "last_touched": d.date().isoformat(), "age_days": age, "older_than_history": False,
861	                      "status": "fresh" if age < 90 else "aging" if age < stale_days else "stale",
862	                      "ancient": age >= 730, "relevant_since": 0, "product_since": 0, "last_commit": "", "evidence": []})
863	    if not pages:
864	        raise RuntimeError("the sitemap has no <lastmod> dates")
865	    pages.sort(key=lambda p: -p["age_days"])
866	    host = re.sub(r"^https?://", "", base)
867	    stale = [p for p in pages if p["status"] == "stale"]
868	    cards = [{"kind": "refresh", "priority": 1 if p["ancient"] else 3, "title": f"Refresh {p['path']}",
869	              "why": f"Last updated {p['last_touched']}, {p['age_days']} days ago. The sitemap gives no product history, so this is age only.",
870	              "action": "Re-read the page, then update or retire it.", "evidence": []} for p in stale[:8]]
871	    cards.append({"kind": "automate", "priority": 3, "title": "Add the source repo for a full audit",
872	                  "why": "With the repo, the audit can tell stale from quiet and list features with no docs.",
873	                  "action": f"firstrun audit owner/repo", "evidence": []})
874	    return {"v": 1, "id": f"audit-{now.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}-{re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', host.lower()).strip('-')}",
875	            "repo": host, "url": base, "generated_at": now.isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "stale_days": stale_days,
876	            "mode": "sitemap", "history": {"commits": 0, "since": "", "capped": False},
877	            "summary": {**_summary(pages), "features": 0, "uncovered": 0, "cards": len(cards)},
878	            "pages": pages[:PAGES_MAX], "release": {"name": "", "previous": "", "date": "", "commits": 0},
879	            "features": [], "cards": cards, "drafts": {"release_notes": "", "highlights": []}, "jev": False,
880	            "cost": {"jev_calls": 0, "jev_input_tokens": 0, "jev_usd": 0.0, "basis": "A sitemap audit makes no model call."}}

898	    return "\n".join(L).rstrip() + "\n"

900	
901	def save(a: dict, out_dir: Path) -> Path:
902	    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
903	    (out_dir / "audit.json").write_text(json.dumps(a, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
904	    (out_dir / "audit.md").write_text(to_markdown(a), encoding="utf-8")
905	    return out_dir / "audit.md"
906	
907	
908	def find_audit_site(start: Path | None = None) -> Path | None:
909	    """docs/audits of the firstrun checkout, found the same way as docs/runs."""
910	    env = os.environ.get("FIRSTRUN_SITE_DIR")
911	    if env:
912	        p = Path(env).parent / "audits"
913	        return p if p.is_dir() else None
914	    here = (start or Path.cwd()).resolve()
915	    for base in [here, *here.parents]:
916	        cand = base / "docs" / "audits"
917	        if (cand / "index.json").exists():
918	            return cand
919	    return None
920	
921	
922	def _receipt(a: dict, site: Path, evidence_dir: Path | None) -> dict:
923	    """Write the audit's receipt into docs/receipts. Returns the index fields, or nothing when it fails."""
924	    from firstrun import receipt
925	
926	    try:
927	        r = receipt.build_audit(a, evidence_dir)
928	        receipt.publish_site(r, site.parent / "receipts")
929	        return receipt.index_fields(r)
930	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a receipt failure never blocks the audit log
931	        return {}
932	
933	
934	def publish(a: dict, site: Path, evidence_dir: Path | None = None) -> Path:
935	    """Write the audit JSON to the site folder, upsert one row in index.json, and write its receipt.
936	
937	    `evidence_dir` is the run folder that holds audit.json and audit.md, when one was saved."""
938	    site.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
939	    out = site / f"{a['id']}.json"
940	    out.write_text(json.dumps(a, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
941	    idx = site / "index.json"
942	    try:
943	        doc = json.loads(idx.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
944	    except (OSError, ValueError):
945	        doc = {}
946	    s = a["summary"]
947	    row = {"id": a["id"], "repo": a["repo"], "url": a["url"], "ts": a["generated_at"], "mode": a.get("mode", "repo"),
948	           "pages": s["pages"], "stale": s["stale"], "quiet": s["quiet"], "oldest_days": s["oldest_days"],
949	           "median_age_days": s["median_age_days"], "features": s["features"], "uncovered": s["uncovered"],
950	           "cards": s["cards"], "release": a["release"]["name"]}
951	    # One current audit per repo: a newer audit replaces the older row and its file.
952	    key = (a["repo"], a.get("docs_repo", ""))
953	    rows = []
954	    for r in doc.get("audits", []):
955	        if r.get("id") != a["id"] and (r.get("repo"), r.get("docs_repo", "")) == key:
956	            (site / f"{r['id']}.json").unlink(missing_ok=True)
957	        elif r.get("id") != a["id"]:
958	            rows.append(r)
959	    row["docs_repo"] = a.get("docs_repo", "")
960	    row.update(_receipt(a, site, evidence_dir))
961	    rows.append(row)
962	    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["ts"], reverse=True)
963	    idx.write_text(json.dumps({"audits": rows}, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
964	    return out
965	
966	
967	def issue(a: dict) -> dict:
968	    """A GitHub issue for the docs team: one checkbox per card, evidence linked, drafts folded."""
969	    s = a["summary"]
970	    url = a.get("url") or ""
971	    L = [f"FirstRun audited the docs of {a['repo']} on {a['generated_at'][:10]}.", "",
972	         f"- {s['pages']} pages: {s['stale']} stale, {s['quiet']} quiet, {s['aging']} aging, {s['fresh']} fresh.",
973	         f"- Oldest page: {s['oldest_days']} days. Median: {s['median_age_days']} days.",
974	         f"- {s['uncovered']} of {s['features']} user-facing features from the last {FEATURE_WINDOW_DAYS} days have no docs page that names them.",
975	         "", "## Proposed Work", ""]
976	    for c in a["cards"]:
977	        if c["kind"] == "quickstart":
978	            continue
979	        L.append(f"- [ ] **{c['title']}**. {c['why']}")
980	        for e in c.get("evidence", [])[:3]:
981	            ref = f"#{e['pr']}" if e.get("pr") else (f"{url}/commit/{e['sha']}" if url else e["sha"])
982	            L.append(f"  - {e['date']}: {e['subject']} ({ref})")
983	    notes = a["drafts"].get("release_notes") or ""
984	    if notes:
985	        L += ["", "<details><summary>Release notes draft</summary>", "", notes, "</details>"]
986	    L += ["", "Stale means product commits on the page's topic landed after its last edit. "
987	          "Quiet pages are old but nothing changed under them.",
988	          "", "_Generated by [FirstRun](https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun) `firstrun audit`._"]
989	    title = f"Docs audit: {s['stale']} stale pages, {s['uncovered']} features with no docs"
990	    body = "\n".join(L)
991	    repo = a["repo"] if "/" in a["repo"] and url else ""
992	    cmd = f"gh issue create --repo {repo} --title \"{title}\" --body-file issue.md" if repo else ""
993	    return {"repo": repo, "title": title, "body": body, "commands": [cmd] if cmd else []}
